shorts.title: Trump on Obama's Detroit rally: "the place was empty" #Shorts

shorts.title: Judge to Trump team: "cost the government all credibility with me" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Friends, over a holiday weekend, at least four hundred trees came down at a public golf course in Washington, D.C. Federal Judge Ana Reyes was not amused. Quote: "What has happened has cost the government all credibility with me." [beat] [incredulous] She wrote that officials rushed because, quote, "President Trump demands haste on his redesign." Trump has said the course would host "Major Golf Tournaments." [beat] Her order halts the cutting through Monday, and demands three business days' written notice before any irreversible change. [deadpan] Three days' notice. For a chainsaw. [beat] Alexander Hamilton, Federalist 78: "The complete independence of the courts of justice is peculiarly essential in a limited Constitution." [sarcastic] Limited. That's the word. [beat] So friends: if the plan was so great, why did it need a long weekend? Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes on Oct. 13, 2026 halted tree-cutting at the East Potomac golf course in Washington, D.C. until Oct. 26; at least 400 trees had been cut over the holiday weekend.
Reyes said at the hearing: "What has happened has cost the government all credibility with me."
Reyes wrote that officials rushed the tree plan because "President Trump demands haste on his redesign."
Trump said in a June social media post that the course would host "Major Golf Tournaments" once completed.
The order requires the government to "provide the court and plaintiffs three business days' written advance notice" before irreparable changes.
Hamilton wrote in Federalist No. 78: "The complete independence of the courts of justice is peculiarly essential in a limited Constitution."

shorts.title: Thune on Trump's ads: "shouldn't be paid for with taxpayer dollars" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [amused] Friends, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a Republican, says the ads "shouldn't be paid for with taxpayer dollars." [beat] Which ads? The ones the Department of Homeland Security bought with twenty million taxpayer dollars, promoting President Trump's midterm message. Federal Judge Jennifer Rochon ordered the remaining spots canceled. The White House calls them public service announcements. [deadpan] Public service. The public being served: Trump. [beat] Trump later said he would pay from a campaign account, but a White House official said there were no immediate plans to repay the money already spent. [sarcastic] Thomas Jefferson, in his 1779 bill for religious freedom: to compel a man to furnish money for opinions he abhors "is sinful and tyrannical." [beat] He never mentioned commercial breaks. Friends, if the ads are so good, why not pay for them yourselves? Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: Senate Majority Leader John Thune said the ads "shouldn't be paid for with taxpayer dollars."
The Department of Homeland Security spent $20 million in taxpayer money on the ads, which promoted Trump and his midterm message.
U.S. District Judge Jennifer L. Rochon granted a two-week temporary restraining order on Oct. 11, 2026 telling the administration to cancel remaining ads.
The White House defended the ads as public service announcements.

shorts.title: Trump on El-Sayed: "He hates our country" — as polls tighten #Shorts
shorts.hook: Trump on El-Sayed: "He hates our country"
shorts.narration: [serious] Friends, President Trump, at the White House, about Michigan's Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. Quote: "He's a Muslim Brotherhood guy. One hundred percent." And: "He hates our country." [beat] That is Trump's allegation. El-Sayed has repeatedly denied ties, and argues the attacks are meant to distract from economic issues. [deadpan] Distract. From the economy. Imagine that. [beat] The Silver Bulletin average, as reported by Newsweek on Friday, has El-Sayed ahead of Republican Mike Rogers, 48.4 to 45.4. [sarcastic] And when the polling looks like that, the label gets louder. [beat] A reminder from Article Six of the Constitution: "no religious Test shall ever be required as a Qualification to any Office or public Trust under the United States." Friends, what is the Republican plan for prices? Michigan wants to know. Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.
